title: UPI-Style Real-Time Payment Gateway with VPA Resolution, Dynamic Bank Routing & T+1 Settlement
problem: Large-scale real-time payment infrastructures like UPI process billions of monthly peer-to-peer and merchant transactions, requiring sub-second response times, multi-bank failover routing, and ironclad financial consistency. Naive payment gateways suffer from double-debiting during network timeouts, race conditions across concurrent wallet balances, and ledger desynchronization during batch settlement failures. This project builds a high-throughput UPI-style payment gateway in Java and Spring Boot with Redis VPA (Virtual Payment Address) resolution, dynamic bank switching heuristics based on live latency and error rates, idempotent payment authorization, PostgreSQL double-entry bookkeeping, and an asynchronous Kafka T+1 net settlement engine.

use_cases.title: High-Volume Peer-to-Merchant (P2M) QR Code Checkout
use_cases.first_sentence: Retail merchants accepting dynamic QR code payments require instant payment authorization and immediate customer notification without pending state lockups.
use_cases.second_sentence: The Spring Boot payment gateway authorizes inbound UPI requests in under 65ms, verifies account balance limits, and publishes payment success events to Kafka.

use_cases.title: Multi-Bank Dynamic Failover Routing during Bank Outages
use_cases.first_sentence: When a major partner bank experiences sudden core banking timeouts, payment success rates across all connected merchant checkouts drop precipitously.
use_cases.second_sentence: The gateway monitors rolling 60-second bank health metrics in Redis and automatically shifts transaction volume to secondary partner bank switches.

use_cases.title: Automated T+1 Merchant Position Netting & Ledger Reconciliation
use_cases.first_sentence: Acquiring banks must compute aggregate gross processing volume, deduct interchange fees, and generate net settlement payout batches every 24 hours.
use_cases.second_sentence: A Kafka streaming batch worker processes daily payment ledger entries, calculates net clearing positions across all merchants, and generates double-entry payout journals.

hard_parts: Enforcing strict idempotency across distributed payment requests using atomic Redis locks and PostgreSQL unique constraint ledgers to prevent double-debits
Implementing an automated double-entry bookkeeping ledger guaranteeing asset-liability equality across all financial state transitions
Designing dynamic multi-bank routing algorithms with circuit breakers shifting traffic away from degraded bank simulator switches
Executing asynchronous T+1 net settlement batch processing with exact financial reconciliation across millions of transaction records
screener_signals: Clean Java / Spring Boot microservice repository cleanly separating VPA resolution, bank adapter interfaces, double-entry ledger services, and Kafka batchers
High-concurrency benchmark report proving sustained processing of 3,500+ transactions per second with p95 latency under 65ms
Anti-fake verification script issuing concurrent duplicate requests with identical idempotency keys and asserting exactly 1 debit and matching ledger entries

architecture.data_flow: A client initiates a payment request with an Idempotency-Key; the gateway validates the key against Redis; the VPA resolver looks up payer and payee bank routing details from Redis cache; the dynamic bank switch router evaluates rolling bank health scores and selects the optimal bank rail; the gateway dispatches payment authorization to the mock bank switch; upon bank confirmation, the double-entry ledger writes an atomic debit-credit transaction in PostgreSQL; an event is emitted to Kafka; the T+1 settlement engine consumes Kafka events to net merchant clearing positions; Prometheus tracks payment latency and bank error rates.
architecture.enforcement_mechanism: Redis SETNX distributed locking combined with PostgreSQL unique constraints on idempotency keys and strict double-entry balance constraints.

targets.target: 100 of 100 duplicate requests resolve with exactly 1 database debit and 0 balance discrepancies

targets.metric: Dynamic Bank Switching Failover Recovery Latency

targets.input: Injected 20% timeout fault into primary bank switch during continuous 500 RPS payment stream

targets.target: Failover triggers within 1.1 seconds with 50 of 50 subsequent transactions routed to Bank B

Understanding of distributed systems principles: idempotency, ACID guarantees, message queues, and caching

environment.gpu: None required (purely CPU, in-memory caching, and relational database bound)
environment.cost: $0 (fully open-source stack using local PostgreSQL, Kafka, and Redis in Docker Desktop)
environment.accounts_keys_quotas: No external bank API keys, merchant merchant IDs, or paid cloud services required
environment.reference_environment: Local 4-core CPU, Docker Desktop (PostgreSQL 15, Redis 7, Kafka 3.4), Java 17+, Maven 3.8+
environment.fallback_path: H2 in-memory database and embedded Redis mock if Docker containers cannot be provisioned

riskiest_component.name: Double-Debit Accounting Inconsistencies from Race Conditions during Bank Timeouts
riskiest_component.mitigation: Wrap ledger mutations in SERIALIZABLE database transactions and enforce distributed Redis locks on idempotency keys.
riskiest_component.fallback: Automated reversal reconciliation daemon scanning pending transactions and issuing offsetting credits.
